question: What memory isolation contract should OpenClaw support for multi-user deployments: gateway-owned user/partition identity, per-agent/workspace-only isolation, or no supported multi-tenant memory boundary for now?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but choosing the identity boundary, default behavior, and migration/legacy policy affects privacy guarantees, persisted memory data, config compatibility, and plugin API contracts.

options.title: Approve structural partition isolation
options.body: Define a gateway-owned partition identity and require all memory store/search/get/auto-recall paths to enforce it with explicit legacy-row and migration policy.

options.title: Narrow to agent/workspace isolation
options.body: Treat user-level tenancy as out of scope for now and only support agent/workspace-scoped memory isolation where current architecture already has stronger ownership signals.

options.title: Defer multi-user memory support
options.body: Document that shared memory plugins are not safe for multi-tenant deployments until a future design is sponsored.

recommendation.title: Approve structural partition isolation
recommendation.body: Define a gateway-owned partition identity and require all memory store/search/get/auto-recall paths to enforce it with explicit legacy-row and migration policy.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans memory plugin boundaries, security defaults, and config/migration policy, and steipete has the strongest current history on those surfaces.
